question: Does rustc codegen (opt-level / codegen-units / LTO) materially move the Detcore deterministic-mode per-syscall coordinator-RPC floor (~13.6us/syscall) that dominates all backends?
answer: NO. The floor is ~69% system/kernel-IPC time (sendto/recvfrom/epoll_wait round-trip) plus cross-thread scheduling latency, and only ~31% user-space CPU. Hermit/detcore is ALREADY built at opt-level=3; the residual codegen levers (cgu 16->1, LTO) act only on that 31% user fraction and typically yield single-digit % on already-opt3 code, so best-case whole-floor improvement is <~5% -- within measurement noise. The real lever is eliminating the per-syscall coordinator round-trip (in-process/shared-memory Detcore fastpath, in-guest RCB via rdpmc), not recompiling the coordinator.
method: CPU-time (user+sys) slope across two N under `hermit run --backend liteinst` (deterministic by default), boxed to K free cores via scratch/run-on-k-free-cores.py; /usr/bin/time -v for user/sys/wall/ctx-switch. The load-independent decision quantity is the user:sys RATIO, not absolute ns (shared loaded host).
